name: Germany
note: Germany in the style of the Russian model tree: democratic government as the historical path and alternatives led by real parties of the data (left, conservative, liberal, national-populist, left-populist); economy (Agenda 2010, the Hartz reforms, the debt brake), energy (nuclear phase-out, the energy transition, Nord Stream, LNG), the Bundeswehr (end of conscription, the Zeitenwende) and foreign policy. Sourced starting spirits in data/spirits/deu.json. Alternatives are a counterfactual.

focuses.name: The direction of the country
focuses.description: Which camp governs the country.

focuses.name: Democratic government
focuses.description: Parties alternate in power through elections, as they historically did.

focuses.name: A turn to the left
focuses.description: Parties of the left (the SPD, the Greens and later Die Linke) gain on wages, welfare and public services.

focuses.name: Unions and voters
focuses.description: Unions and young voters rally to the left.

focuses.name: A left-wing government
focuses.description: The most popular party of the democratic left leads the government.

focuses.name: Expand the welfare state
focuses.description: Public health care and higher pensions.

focuses.name: A conservative turn
focuses.description: Conservative parties (the CDU and the CSU) gain on order, tax cuts and tradition.

focuses.name: Business and the countryside
focuses.description: Business and rural voters rally to the right.

focuses.name: A conservative government
focuses.description: The most popular conservative party leads the government.

focuses.name: Fiscal discipline
focuses.description: Cut spending and taxes to balance the budget.

focuses.name: A liberal turn
focuses.description: Liberal parties (the FDP) gain ground on reform and civil liberties.

focuses.name: Reform agenda
focuses.description: A programme of deregulation and civil liberties.

focuses.name: A liberal government
focuses.description: The most popular liberal party leads the government.

focuses.name: Liberal reforms
focuses.description: Cut red tape and open markets.

focuses.name: A populist wave
focuses.description: National-populist parties (the Republicans, the NPD and later the AfD) gain on immigration and sovereignty.

focuses.name: Rallies and referendums
focuses.description: Mass rallies and calls for referendums.

focuses.name: A national-populist government
focuses.description: The most popular national-populist party leads the government.

focuses.name: Sovereignty first
focuses.description: Restrict immigration and limit the power of international bodies.

focuses.name: A socialist turn
focuses.description: Socialist and communist parties (later the BSW) gain in a crisis.

focuses.name: Strikes and occupations
focuses.description: Strikes and workplace occupations.

focuses.name: A socialist government
focuses.description: The most popular socialist party leads the government.

focuses.name: Public ownership
focuses.description: Nationalise the banks and the largest companies.

focuses.name: Economic reform
focuses.description: Make the economy and the welfare state fit for the new century.

focuses.name: Agenda 2010
focuses.description: Reform the welfare state and the labour market, as Chancellor Schröder announced on 14 March 2003.

focuses.name: The Hartz reforms
focuses.description: Reform the job centres and unemployment benefits; the first laws took force on 1 January 2003.

focuses.name: The Mittelstand
focuses.description: Support the family firms that make machines for export.

focuses.name: The debt brake
focuses.description: Limit the federal structural deficit, as the constitution has done since 2009.

focuses.name: Export champions
focuses.description: Cars, chemicals and machines for world markets.

focuses.name: Industry 4.0
focuses.description: Digital factories and robots.

focuses.name: Short-time work
focuses.description: Pay firms to keep workers in a recession.

focuses.name: A minimum wage
focuses.description: A national minimum wage.

focuses.name: Rebuild infrastructure
focuses.description: Bridges, railways and broadband.

focuses.name: Electric cars
focuses.description: Turn the car industry to electric cars.

focuses.name: Chip factories
focuses.description: Subsidise new chip factories.

focuses.name: Skilled immigration
focuses.description: Bring in skilled workers from abroad.

focuses.name: Energy policy
focuses.description: The energy mix for the coming decades.

focuses.name: Nuclear phase-out
focuses.description: Close the nuclear plants: the government decided after Fukushima in 2011, and the last plants closed in April 2023.

focuses.name: The energy transition
focuses.description: Wind and solar replace nuclear and coal. Unlocks offshore wind farms.

focuses.name: Nord Stream
focuses.description: A gas pipeline from Russia under the Baltic, in service from 2011.

focuses.name: Exit from coal
focuses.description: End coal power by 2038 at the latest.

focuses.name: LNG terminals
focuses.description: Terminals for liquefied gas after Russian gas stopped in 2022.

focuses.name: Hydrogen
focuses.description: A national hydrogen strategy.

focuses.name: The Bundeswehr
focuses.description: Reform the armed forces.

focuses.name: Suspend conscription
focuses.description: Suspend conscription, as Germany did on 1 July 2011.

focuses.name: Missions abroad
focuses.description: Deploy to Kosovo, Afghanistan and Mali.

focuses.name: Zeitenwende
focuses.description: Announce a €100 billion fund for the armed forces, as Chancellor Scholz did on 27 February 2022. Unlocks procurement.

focuses.name: Air defence for Europe
focuses.description: A European air-defence shield.

focuses.name: A brigade in Lithuania
focuses.description: Station a brigade permanently in Lithuania.

focuses.name: Ammunition and tanks
focuses.description: Expand ammunition and tank production.

focuses.name: Foreign policy
focuses.description: Germany in Europe and the world.

focuses.name: EU enlargement
focuses.description: Support the entry of Central and Eastern Europe into the EU.

focuses.name: The Franco-German engine
focuses.description: Lead the EU together with France.

focuses.name: Rescue the eurozone
focuses.description: Rescue funds for Greece and others in the debt crisis.

focuses.name: Take in refugees
focuses.description: Take in refugees in the crisis of 2015, when about 1.3 million people applied for asylum in Europe.

focuses.name: Support for Ukraine
focuses.description: Weapons and money for Ukraine.

focuses.name: Trade with China
focuses.description: Cars and machines for China.

focuses.name: Society and science
focuses.description: Health, schools, research and the infrastructure of everyday life.

focuses.name: Invest in hospitals
focuses.description: New hospitals and more doctors.

focuses.name: Invest in schools
focuses.description: Smaller classes and better-paid teachers.

focuses.name: A research agency
focuses.description: Grants for breakthrough research.

focuses.name: Care for the elderly
focuses.description: Care homes and home care for an ageing population.

focuses.name: Leading universities
focuses.description: Funding for the top universities.

focuses.name: Artificial intelligence and computing
focuses.description: Supercomputers and data centres.

focuses.name: Affordable housing
focuses.description: Build homes the young can afford.

focuses.name: Broadband everywhere
focuses.description: Fast internet in every town and village.

focuses.name: Space and satellites
focuses.description: Satellites for navigation and observation.

focuses.name: Public transport

focuses.name: A digital state

focuses.name: Biotechnology

focuses.name: Climate adaptation
focuses.description: Flood defences and water management.
